title: Atlas DataFlow External Analysis Handoff
description: Project Spec S0155. Strict, versioned envelope describing a producer-owned external analysis package before Atlas trusts, inspects, or projects any of its artifacts. This schema governs the handoff document only -- it does not authorize Atlas to consume, copy, or promote any external package, and it does not by itself grant trust: a caller of pipeline/external_analysis_handoff.py must separately supply an explicit trusted-source confirmation before any artifact declared here is considered load-eligible. Dataset identity, source fingerprint, and readiness are explicit typed fields and must never be inferred from a directory name or a model filename. Operational readiness fields are fixed to their safe, unresolved defaults at the schema level: an external handoff can never structurally declare itself operationally ready or carry an operational threshold -- only a later, separately authorized Atlas spec can promote operational readiness.

schema_version.description: Schema version for the external analysis handoff envelope.

artifact_type.description: Explicit artifact type identifying this document as an external analysis handoff, distinct from any internal Atlas contract.

handoff_id.description: Stable identifier for this handoff/package instance. Equivalent in responsibility to a package_id. Must not be a local filesystem path or directory name.

package_id.description: Optional producer-assigned package identifier, distinct from handoff_id when the producer versions handoffs and packages independently.

producer.description: Identity of the producer project. Must be an explicit declaration, not inferred from a directory name.

producer_name.description: Human-readable producer name, e.g. the study or project name.

producer_repository_reference.description: Optional portable reference to the producer repository or study (e.g. a project slug or relative label). Must not be an absolute local path or current Git working-tree path.

consumer.description: Identity of Atlas as the consumer of this handoff.

consumer_system.description: Fixed identifier declaring Atlas DataFlow as the consumer.

consumer_component.description: The Atlas component or boundary that will read this handoff, e.g. 'pipeline.external_analysis_handoff'.

dataset_identity.description: Explicit dataset identity. Must never be inferred solely from a directory name or model filename.

dataset_slug.description: Stable dataset identifier, explicitly declared by the producer.

source_identity.description: Source dataset/analysis identity and fingerprint. Must never embed an absolute local source path.

source_dataset_ref.description: Explicit, reviewable reference to the source dataset or study. Not an absolute local filesystem path.

source_fingerprint.description: Deterministic fingerprint of the source dataset or analysis, carried without any absolute local path.

value.description: Fingerprint value, e.g. a hex-encoded hash. Not a local path.

profile.description: Named fingerprint profile identifying how 'value' was computed and how it must be interpreted.

generated_at.description: Optional timestamp identifying when the source fingerprint was computed.

artifact_inventory.description: Typed inventory of concrete artifact entries. Stable roles and concrete file entries only -- never a broad directory authorization.

trusted_source_declaration.description: The producer's own trust assertion. This declaration alone is never sufficient to trust the source -- pipeline/external_analysis_handoff.py requires a separate, explicit trusted-source confirmation supplied by the caller before any opaque artifact can be considered load-eligible.

producer_asserts_trusted.description: The producer's own assertion of trustworthiness. Informational only; never sufficient to authorize load-eligibility by itself.

basis.description: Basis for the producer's trust assertion.

readiness.description: Readiness declarations. Educational and operational readiness are kept structurally distinct so an educational-only package can never be promoted to operational readiness through this schema.

educational_modeling_complete.description: Whether the producer's educational modeling work is complete.

educational_threshold.description: Educational threshold evidence preserved as declared, or null when none was declared. Never reclassified as an operational threshold.

basis.description: Basis for the educational readiness declaration.

operational.description: Fixed to safe, unresolved defaults. An external handoff cannot structurally declare itself operationally ready.

operational_limitations.description: Explicit operational limitations disclosed by the producer or Atlas boundary (e.g. runtime compatibility unresolved, no operational threshold defined).

package_is_immutable.description: Declares that the referenced package content is immutable once handed off.

basis.description: Basis for the immutability declaration (e.g. content-addressed hashing of every inventoried artifact).

generated_at.description: Optional timestamp identifying when this handoff document was produced.

safe_relative_reference.description: Portable relative reference. Rejects absolute POSIX paths, Windows drive paths, UNC/backslash paths, parent traversal, empty and dot-only paths, and repeated separators.

artifact_entry.description: A single, concrete artifact entry. Content is never trusted or deserialized based on this declaration alone -- pipeline/external_analysis_handoff.py revalidates every field against the real package root.

required.description: Whether this artifact must be present for the package to validate.

content_kind.description: Declares how this artifact must be treated. Only json_evidence/json_manifest artifacts are ever parsed as JSON. opaque_model_artifact is never deserialized by the handoff validator.

sha256.description: Declared byte SHA-256 of this artifact. Recomputed by streaming bytes; validation fails on divergence.

semantic_fingerprint.description: Optional producer-declared semantic fingerprint (e.g. a model-state fingerprint). Never recomputed by loading an opaque artifact -- only cross-checked across declared JSON artifacts.

profile.description: Named semantic fingerprint profile. An unsupported profile must fail closed rather than being silently accepted.
